note: RM-004 follow-on: the last opaque PNG on the GPU path, re-encoded as JPEG.
P6 converted 21 opaque PNGs for this reason and missed this one. Once B4
resized the large JPEGs it became the largest file served - 476 KB for a
512x512 texture, 1.861 bytes per texel, nine times the density of any JPEG
in the catalog. 18 KB of that was metadata: an embedded ICC profile and a
Lossless was measured first and rejected: re-deflating the pixels without
the metadata produces 564 KB, LARGER than the original, so whatever wrote
this file compressed it better than a plain re-encode can.
It is colour type 2 with no tRNS chunk - no alpha to lose. The four PNGs
left on the GPU path all carry real alpha and correctly stay PNG.
The rename is the interesting part. This is the DEFAULT room texture, so
its logical name is written into saved designs, and A5 made an asset URL in
a document a name rather than an address. The manifest carries a retired
entry pointing the old name at the new file - the first use of an
indirection A5 built and nothing had needed until now.
